candidates.name: Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DRESS)
support_spans: marked leukocytosis, hyperglycemia, hypoproteinemia, transaminitis, and an elevated C‐reactive protein level
separation of the stratum corneum with multifocal subcorneal collections of neutrophils, underlying spongiotic epidermis with neutrophilic exocytosis
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory results are consistent with DRESS, a severe drug reaction that can occur after re-exposure to a medication.

candidates.name: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS)
support_spans: separation of the stratum corneum with multifocal subcorneal collections of neutrophils
contradict_spans: resolved over three months following drug discontinuation and corticosteroid therapy
candidates.why: The patient's skin symptoms and histopathological findings are consistent with SJS, a severe cutaneous adverse reaction.

candidates.name: Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN)
support_spans: separation of the stratum corneum with multifocal subcorneal collections of neutrophils
contradict_spans: resolved over three months following drug discontinuation and corticosteroid therapy
candidates.why: The patient's skin symptoms and histopathological findings are consistent with TEN, a severe skin condition that can be caused by medication.

key_evidence_spans: A 70‐year‐old woman with an undifferentiated connective tissue disorder and rheumatoid arthritis was treated with hydroxychloroquine
Three days after restarting the drug, she was admitted with widespread erythema, desquamation, and pustulation
Skin biopsies from the back demonstrated separation of the stratum corneum with multifocal subcorneal collections of neutrophils
